title: Boundaries 3: Check Commas and Finish the Routine
description: Follow Full Stop → Colon → Dash → Comma, choosing and stopping when a candidate passes. Check serial semicolons within the first stage, then use specific yes/no tests for comma jobs and no punctuation.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The baker packed ______ rolls, and cookies for the market.
questions.explanation_html: The words on both sides of the blank name separate items in a simple list. A comma separates those items.
questions.variation: Separate ordinary list items with a comma

distractor_notes.A: Makes an unfinished phrase stand on its own.
distractor_notes.B: Uses a colon before words that do not explain or specify the introduction.

questions.stem_html: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
questions.stimulus_html: The three guests came from Lyon, ______ Turin, Italy; and Porto, Portugal.
questions.explanation_html: The list names three groups. Because the individual items already contain commas, a semicolon separates the first complete item from the second.
questions.variation: Separate complex list items with semicolons

distractor_notes.A: Splits the list before the remaining items.
distractor_notes.B: The last items do not explain the place or name before the blank.
distractor_notes.D: Adds the final-item conjunction too early.
